title: AI character replacement for video ad localization
summary: Replace your ad spokesperson for each market using AI, no reshoot needed. Full workflow using Magic Hour's Character Replace and Lip Sync tools.
body_markdown:
## Quick answer


**AI character replacement can adapt the on-screen person in an existing ad, while voice, lip sync, captions, and copy may require separate localization steps.**


Start with approved source footage and permission covering each person’s likeness and market use.[Magic Hour’s character-replace tool](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) handles the visual workflow; review the finished version with someone who understands the target language and market.


## **The Problem With Traditional Ad Localization**


Localizing an ad may involve new voice recordings, translated copy, captions, graphics, talent agreements and edits. A new shoot adds casting, crew, travel and studio costs when those are needed. Reusing approved footage can avoid some of that work, but changing the presenter is only useful if it serves the campaign and the people who will see it.


That timeline also creates a media problem: by the time every localized version is ready, part of the campaign window may already be gone. AI character replacement offers a different model by keeping the original shoot and adapting the on-screen talent after production.


## **What AI Character Replacement Actually Does in an Ad Context**


Marketers often group character replacement, dubbing, and AI avatars together, but they solve different problems.


### **Character Replace vs Dubbing vs AI Avatars**


**Approach**


**What It Does**


**Best For**


**AI Dubbing / Lip Sync only**


Keeps the original spokesperson and syncs new audio to their mouth movements


When the original talent is appropriate for all markets


**AI Avatar**


Generates a virtual presenter from scratch


When no original footage exists


**AI Character Replace**


Swaps the original spokesperson with a local face while keeping the original performance


When you want a local face in existing footage without reshooting


A different presenter may help when research or a campaign brief calls for that person, character or mascot. Appearance alone does not establish cultural relevance. First check whether language, the offer, examples or product availability are the actual localization problem; changing those may be enough.


## **The Workflow: One Shoot, Multiple Market Versions**


### **1. Shoot Once With Any On-Camera Talent**


The hero production can remain straightforward: one spokesperson, one set, one production day, and one finished commercial. That source footage becomes the foundation for every regional version, so its lighting, framing, camera movement, and performance quality set the ceiling for the final outputs.


### **2. Replace the Spokesperson for Each Market**


Upload the approved source video and a reference image to[Magic Hour Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . Use the replacement workflow to change the main subject while retaining the shot. Inspect the result for changes to the performance, product and background; preservation is a goal to verify, not a guarantee for every frame. The[step-by-step character replacement guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-replace-a-character-in-a-video-with-ai-for-free) covers input preparation.


Check the accepted clip length and credit estimate in the current uploader before planning the edit. Work shot by shot where needed. Magic Hour’s paid plans include commercial use and watermark-free video exports; the free tool is for testing.


### **3. Sync Localized Audio**


The next layer is language. Upload the character-replaced video to[Magic Hour Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) along with the dubbed audio for the target market, and the tool synchronizes the replacement spokesperson's mouth movements to the new track.


This separates the visual localization problem from the language problem: Character Replace changes who appears on screen, while Lip Sync adapts how that person speaks. A dedicated[AI lip sync guide](https://magichour.ai/blog/how-to-lip-sync-a-video-with-ai) can cover the audio workflow in more detail.


### **4. Review and Export**


Review identity and wardrobe across frames, mouth timing, product details, captions, offer accuracy and the background. Have a fluent reviewer check the finished voice and copy in context. A paid tool license covers the platform’s commercial-use permission; it does not supply talent releases, music rights or approval of an advertising claim.


## **Where This Works Best (And Where It Has Limits)**


### **Where It Works Best**


- Clearly framed spokesperson footage with a consistent background.
- Short, separate shots that fit the uploader’s current limits.
- Campaigns with an approved reason to change the presenter or mascot.
- A/B tests that keep the offer, script and placement consistent while comparing one creative change.


### **Current Limitations to Know Before You Pitch This Internally**


- **Duration and cost:** confirm the selected workflow’s current upload limit and generation quote; a finished ad can contain several separately processed shots.
- **Difficult footage:** fast motion, occlusion and interacting subjects can cause unstable replacements.
- **Reference quality:** match the subject’s framing and lighting to the source clip where possible.
- **Rights and review:** budget for the paid commercial workflow, talent permissions, localization and final approval—not just generation credits.


## Example Uses to Evaluate


- Replace a US-based spokesperson with a local presenter for a regional launch without rebooking talent or studio time.
- Test two different spokesperson looks in the same 10-second ad before committing production budget to either.
- Update a training or onboarding video after a spokesperson leaves the company without recreating the original recording.
- Create market-specific product demos where the presenter matches the demographic of each target audience.
- Build a campaign concept deck showing different talent directions in the same footage before a client approves casting.


## Compare the Cost of an Approved Market Version


### **Traditional multi-market production:**


- Additional talent, crew, travel and studio costs if a new shoot is required.
- Translation, voice recording, editing, captions and regional review.
- Any reshoot or revision needed before approval.


### **AI character replacement workflow:**


- Source-footage preparation and permissions.
- Character-replacement attempts, including rejected outputs.
- Dubbed audio, lip sync, captions and manual cleanup.
- Local review, revisions and final approval.


Compare **total production and review spend ÷ approved market versions** , using the same scope for both approaches. For example, five market versions with three shots each and two attempts per shot require 30 character-replacement generations before audio or revisions. That is a planning example, not a measured cost saving or a prediction of the number of attempts you will need.


## **What to Try Next**

If you only need to replace a face while keeping the original person's body and clothing,[Magic Hour Face Swap Video](https://magichour.ai/products/face-swap/video) is the more precise option. Both tools run in the browser without additional software.


## Frequently Asked Questions


###


Magic Hour's paid plans permit commercial use of generated outputs. You also need the appropriate rights or model release for any real person used as the replacement reference; using someone's likeness without consent is not made permissible simply because AI generated the video.


###


The strongest results come from clear, well-lit footage paired with a professional reference photo. Fast movement, heavy occlusion, and complex interactions can make the replacement less stable. Generate a representative proof first, then stop only when one result passes the defined frame, identity, product, background and motion checks; an arbitrary number of variations does not establish quality.


###


Use the format required by the placement—often vertical for Reels, TikTok and Shorts—and check the current upload and output settings. There is no single clip limit established here for every Character Replace plan or workflow. For a longer ad, process suitable shots individually and assemble the approved clips in your editor.


###


Timing depends on clip length, output settings, queue load and the number of attempts. The finished market version also needs audio, captions, editing and local review. Time one representative shot end to end before scheduling a campaign; a generation-time estimate is not an approval deadline.


###


The replacement workflow is intended to retain the source scene while changing the primary subject. The current tool exposes **Replace** and **Animate** options, so confirm the selected mode before spending credits. Compare the generated background against the source, especially around hands, hair and moving objects; reject or repair unintended changes.


For ads, document who approved the source performance and replacement likeness, the exact script and claim, each target market, and who performs local review. The FTC’s[current testimonial-rule guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) explains U.S. endorsement and testimonial responsibilities; other markets and platforms can impose different rules. Use the[face-swap ads checklist](https://magichour.ai/blog/face-swap-for-ads) for the rights, claim, disclosure and audit steps before launch.


### Create one reviewed localization draft


Use approved source footage and a permitted reference character. Generate one representative market version, then review the performance, product, claims, disclosure, captions and complete export.
